name: Renewal Reminder Ladder with Risk Scoring

parameters.content:
## Renewal Reminder Ladder with Risk Scoring

Chasing renewals by hand means someone has to read a spreadsheet every
morning and remember who was already contacted. This workflow does that
scan for you and walks each customer up a three step reminder ladder,
so nobody gets the same nudge twice and nobody is missed.

### How it works

Every morning the workflow reads your renewal sheet and cleans the rows,
accepting several common date formats and skipping anything unusable. A
code step works out how many days are left, places each customer on the
T-30, T-7 or T-1 rung, and drops anyone who already received that rung.
The same step builds a risk score from product usage, open support
tickets, contract value and how close the date is. Customers are then
handled one at a time: an AI model writes a short email whose tone
matches the risk tier, Gmail sends it, and the sheet is updated with the
rung, the date and the score so the next run stays accurate. Renewals
scoring seventy or above also get a save call booked on the account
owner's calendar. At the end, one Slack message summarises the batch and
lists the accounts that need a human.

### Setup

Connect Google Sheets, Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack and your AI model
credentials. Put your sheet ID in both Sheets nodes and set the tab name
to the tab holding your renewals. Set the Slack channel and the owner
calendar. Adjust the trigger hour, the ladder day ranges and the risk
score weights to match how your team sells.

### Customization

Swap Gmail for your own mail provider, replace Slack with Microsoft
Teams, or change the risk threshold that books a save call.

## Daily scan and ladder logic
Reads the renewal sheet each morning, cleans the rows, works out days left, places each customer on a reminder rung and scores the renewal risk.

## One customer at a time
Writes a short email in a tone that matches the risk tier, sends it, records the rung and score back in the sheet, and books a save call for high risk renewals.

## Daily summary for the team
Once the batch finishes, one Slack message reports how many reminders went out at each rung and which accounts need a human this week.

options.systemMessage:
You write short renewal reminder emails on behalf of a B2B software company.

Rules:
- Keep the body under 130 words and use plain sentences.
- Never invent prices, discounts, features or dates that are not in the input.
- Mention the renewal date exactly as given.
- Match the tone you are asked for. Do not use exclamation marks.
- Close with one clear next step: confirm the renewal, or reply to book a short call.
- Write the body as plain text with line breaks, no markdown and no signature block.
- Return only the JSON fields you are asked for.
